PRIMARY.pick: DD2 lifecycle-intel, SaaS-only (C-80 + C-29 + C-61 LTB sizer and studies), run as a gated side business. It is not a venture: it never pays the founder in 36 months.
PRIMARY.rationale: This is the highest-EV option in the pool, but only by a small margin, and its edge comes from option value, not from a strong point estimate. (1) Revised economics (04_DEEPDIVES/lifecycle-intel.md §14.3; models/lifecycle-intel.py §6, re-run exit 0): first revenue m6 (2027-05). ARR $69,915 at m18 and $149,629 at m36 in BASE, $104,077 in GLUT, $83,031 in SEVERE. Breakeven with the founder unpaid at m17. Cash low $6,100 at m16, a $33,900 draw. The $10k/month salary is never covered in any scenario. 36-month cash change is +$36.4k BASE, +$6.8k GLUT and -$8.9k SEVERE. (2) It has the largest sellable recurring asset among the survivors: pure software at 57% GM by m36. Its EOL/lifecycle module holds flat at $5,774/month through the glut (model §6). DD5 reaches only $41.2k/$65.7k ARR and is 60-70% services, and DD1/DD3/DD4/DD6/DD7 have negative or ~zero EV (phase5 ev_notes). (3) It has the cheapest decisive test in the set: ~$2,950, 29 days, ~55 h, with no code before K0 (§10). (4) Two other options ride along at ~$0 extra cost: the C-86 index (K3/K4) and the C-72 co-op (three supplier calls). My EV [ESTIMATE; scratch calc]: I put P(K0)=0.6, P(K6|K0)=0.5 and P(K1)=0.35, so P(pass) is ~0.10. I weight BASE/GLUT/SEVERE at 0.35/0.45/0.20, value the business at the end at 3x SDE with a 50% haircut, apply a K5-fail factor, and assume 40% of passing worlds stop early at about -$20k. That gives E[cash] of about +$4k and E[hours] of about 207. Net of time at $25/h it is about -$1k. That is indistinguishable from keeping the day job (EV 0), but the downside is capped at about $3k and 55 h before the first hard gate. If K0 fails, the correct PRIMARY is NONE (keep the day job and the $40k). It becomes a salary-paying PRIMARY only on a K1 strong pass. That means at least 8 of 25 deposits and at least 4 paying accounts at m9, which fits the >=14.7% conversion the model needs. The model's conversion-0.15 run reaches $318k ARR and full-time at m33 in BASE, but never in GLUT.
PRIMARY.gate: Gate 1, K0 by 2026-11-09: a written employer carve-out covering the product, the SMB-OEM industry and third-party PO-price contributions. If it is refused, stop everything and do nothing. Gates 2 and 3 by 2026-12-01: K6 (25 qualified calls booked within 21 days from cold outreach outside the employer's network) and K1 (at least 5 of 25 give a refundable $500 deposit or a paid LOI at >=$200/month). Either failing kills DD2. K5 by 2026-12-15: Nexar or DigiKey allows in-app price display at <=$1,000/month. If not, re-run K1 on a demo built on public prints; if that fails, kill. After a pass: at least 2 paying accounts by 2027-08-31 (m9); at least 5 accounts or MRR >=$1,700 by 2027-11-30 (m12); stop if cash falls below $5k; at least 13 accounts by m18, or open exit talks with Lytica, Z2Data, Accuris or Luminovo.
PRIMARY.spend: Week of 2026-11-02: at most $500, for an employment-agreement review (K0). Only after K0 is signed: at most about $1,450 more through 2026-12-01 (Sales Navigator ~$100, 25 x $50 call thank-yous, domain ~$100). Defer the $1,000 government-contracts attorney consult and the model's $5,000 m2 antitrust opinion until K3+K4 pass, because both protect only the index panel. The model charges the $5k opinion unconditionally, so deferring it raises the BASE cash low from $6.1k to about $11k [ESTIMATE]. Hard cap on the test: $5,000. If it passes, put in at most ~$20k through the m9 gate and at most $34k in total ever, and never go below a $5k cash floor.

FALLBACK.pick: DD5 open-memory-ip, C-33 OpenRAM macro service wedge only (sky130/GF180), run in sequence: free legs first, and only if DD2 fails.
FALLBACK.rationale: No candidate is a safe path to meaningful revenue. DD5 is the safest in the bounded-downside, cycle-proof sense, and its buyers are open-PDK tapeout teams, not SMB-OEM procurement, so it does not share DD2's main failure mode. Per 04_DEEPDIVES/open-memory-ip.md §14.3 and models/open-memory-ip.py: ARR is $41.2k at m18 and $65.7k at m36 in BASE ($54.9k GLUT, $49.3k SEVERE), so a DDR5 glut cuts it only ~16%. Cash flow breaks even at m12 with the founder unpaid, and gross margin is 57%. It is the only survivor whose 36-month cash, conditional on passing, is positive in all three price decks: end cash $88.4k, $60.4k and $45.1k from $40k. A cash gate keeps the low at $4.0k (m15). It never pays a salary. A full free release cuts m36 ARR to $34.0k. It depends on one exclusive contract memory engineer. It is also the only survivor tied to U.S.-fab silicon (sky130 at SkyWater; GF180 is fabbed in Singapore). The author puts the pass probability at 15-25% (phase5 ev_note: about +$5-15k EV before time). I put it nearer 10%, because test (iv) asks open-source maintainers for a written no-release promise and silence counts as FAIL. Sequenced so that the $0 legs come first, my EV is about +$1.5k cash, or about -$3k at $25/h [ESTIMATE]. That is worse than DD2: a 3x costlier test, a services-heavy revenue mix and a hard-to-sell asset at the end. So it is the fallback, not the primary.
FALLBACK.gate: In order: (iv) written statements from BOTH UCSC VLSIDA and Open Circuit Design that they have no plan to release silicon-characterized >=16 KB open macros within 18 months, or a signed exclusivity; no answer = FAIL. (ii) At least 2 commercial or SBIR buyers commit at >=$10k each, staying on the open PDK and accepting a licence of nominal-lot measured, corners simulated, refund-capped warranty. Only then (iii): a contractor-signed extracted-SPICE corner run plus a >=1,000-point Monte Carlo on the 16 KB sky130 macro, with <=200 h to build the full line. And (i): at least 3 paid $500 deposits against >=$2k orders, or >=$15k of LOIs from distinct funded teams. Afterwards: an exclusive contractor SOW or technical cofounder by m3, and >=$4k invoiced by m6. Kill on any miss of (i), (iii) or (iv).
FALLBACK.spend: Nov 2026: $0 and at most 5 h. Send the step-4 written questions (UCSC, OCD, ChipFoundry, wafer.space, Cadence, Synopsys-GF) while DD2's test runs, and buy nothing. Only if DD2 fails on 2026-12-01 AND both no-release statements are in writing: in Jan-Feb 2027 (spring term), spend at most $1.5k on the page, refundable deposits and the licence template. Commission the $6.0k, 40-h contractor review only after 2 LOIs of >=$10k exist. Cap: $9.1k. After that, the model's $2.5k cash-floor gate governs spending. If DD2 passes, DD5 stays parked, because 15 h/week cannot staff both.

MOONSHOT.pick: NONE qualifies. The best available option is C-86 (Memory Cost Escalation Index + EPA clause kit), held as a K3/K4-gated option inside DD2's kill test.
MOONSHOT.rationale: Every T2+ path is dead or out of reach for this founder. C-32 (gain cell) and C-22 (ReRAM) were killed: neither has a density or leakage case on sky130, and the ReRAM's only selling point, magnetic immunity, is matched by OTP, eFuse and S130's own eNVM (open-memory-ip.md §14). DD7's Plan B returns 0.29x on $11.49M, its BULL case is about 22%/yr gross over 10 years, and the MCM must be redesigned (legacy-dram-diebank.md §14.3). All 24 T3/T4 concepts died in Phase 3. The best surviving T2 concept, C-36 (Fab 25 SRAM second source), was never deep-dived: it ranks #20 under moonshot weighting, has founder-fit 1, would fight Infineon, the anchor customer of the same fab, and needs $5-15M (03_SCORING.md §7.8). 03_SCORING.md §6 says the only credible path above $2M among the top 15 is C-86 becoming the contract reference index (upside $2-10M ARR). The red team killed the SaaS-fed version, since the panel reaches only 14.2 members against the 15 needed by m36, and found no glut hedge (lifecycle-intel.md §14). Even 10 seeded contributors add only $15-25k of m36 ARR (model §10: $165k-$174k vs $150k). So it qualifies only as a long-horizon call option, which A-12 allows a MOONSHOT to be. Its incremental cost is about $0, because the K3/K4 asks ride on DD2's 25 calls. Probability that it ever qualifies: about 3% [ESTIMATE]. Confidence below is confidence that NONE is the right verdict.
MOONSHOT.gate: C-86 qualifies only if both pass by 2026-12-01. K3: at least 2 of 10 signed LOIs that name a live contract or surcharge schedule which will cite the index, each saying why TrendForce contract prints and open-book pass-through don't serve. K4: at least 10 contribution agreements signed by the buyer's legal function, each covering line-item POs and >=$250k/yr of memory spend, not EMS-turnkey, with >=70% of spend in <=4 grade-homogeneous cells. It must then pass the VET-01 statistical test by m9. By 2028-02-29 (m15) it needs >=15 panel members with usable histories, or one executed contract between unaffiliated parties naming the index. Otherwise the option closes for good. C-36 would qualify as a hardware moonshot only if a SRAM or hi-rel cofounder arrives with written SkyWater Fab 25 outside-customer 6T-bitcell PDK access, a named prime LOI and T2 capital. The founder spends $0 on that.
MOONSHOT.spend: $0 now beyond DD2's test. Spend the deferred $1,000 attorney consult and the $5,000 antitrust opinion only after K3+K4 pass. Spend nothing further until an executed contract names the index.

honest_framing: For a founder with under $50k, the study's answer to 'make RAM, or something better, in America' is no. Incumbent DDR5 costs about $1.48/GB to make against a $20.37/GB contract price, and still earns about 82% gross margin at the $8.15/GB glut price. No alternative memory comes within 10x on $/GB. The U.S. has no DRAM foundry, no display fab and no open die supply, and buyers pay no general Made-in-USA premium for memory (01_LANDSCAPE.md §0). Every device path above T1 died: 24 T3/T4 concepts in Phase 3, then C-32, C-22, C-91 and C-65 in red team. Of the seven deep dives, five were killed and two downgraded (186 objections, 0 refuted), and nothing pays the founder a salary within 36 months in any price scenario. What survives is software sold to people who buy memory, chiefly DD2 at about $70k ARR at m18 and $150k at m36. That is a side business, not a venture, and it does not make anything. Re-aim the project now: drop manufacturing as the business goal (that is Micron's T4 game, backed by $6.1B of CHIPS money), treat the next 30 days as a $3k-or-less option on a memory-lifecycle SaaS for SMB hardware OEMs, and if K0, K1 or K6 fails, keep the day job and the $40k, and look outside memory for a venture where the founder's software speed is the moat.
biggest_unknown: The study's biggest unknown is whether any memory-adjacent buyer will pay this part-time founder recurring money at all. All seven deep dives died on willingness to pay, moat or channel, not on physics. The cheapest observable test of it is DD2's K1: will at least 5 of 25 cold-sourced SMB hardware-OEM procurement leads put down a refundable $500 deposit or sign a paid LOI at >=$200/month, for alerts that Octopart, DigiKey and $250 SiliconExpert partly give away? K1 also stands in for the >=14.7% conversion that would ever pay a salary. One binary gate sits upstream of it: the employer's written carve-out (K0).
